checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322
checked_sources.result: Primary reference for non-partitioned aggregation: point-null e-processes over candidate changepoints, outer infimum over no-change laws, unit-weight aggregation for ARL and summable start weights for PFA. Its PFA delay includes the changepoint-time prior penalty, asymptotically log T plus lower-order terms.

checked_sources.source: Shin, Ramdas & Rinaldo 2022/2024, E-detectors: a nonparametric framework for sequential change detection
checked_sources.result: Primary e-detector reference: sums of delayed e-processes give ARL control; summable initial weights give the stronger probability-of-false-alarm control. This distinction is essential for the frozen-anchor boundary derived here.

checked_sources.source: Ruf, Larsson, Koolen & Ramdas 2023, A composite generalization of Ville's martingale theorem using e-processes
checked_sources.result: Supports the composite-null e-process principle used below: if a process is pointwise dominated by a valid null-specific test martingale/supermartingale for every null law, the infimum construction is anytime-valid for the composite null.

checked_sources.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen 2024, Safe testing
checked_sources.result: Independent reference for likelihood-ratio/test-martingale optional-stopping validity and Ville-style threshold control.

derived_results.claim: The frozen-anchor segmented architecture has a clean composite-null PFA theorem with deterministic sparse starts, without interchanging the outer infimum and the start mixture.
derived_results.statement: Let P be the no-change class. For deterministic candidate splits s_k, let Q_k be any proper infinite-horizon predictive law whose pre-split predictor is frozen/common as desired and whose post-split predictor resets at s_k. For R in P, L^R_{k,t}=dQ_k^(t)/dR^(t) is a nonnegative R-martingale. Let e_k be a deterministic expiry and define killed wealth Ltilde^R_{k,t}=L^R_{k,t} for t<e_k and 0 thereafter; this is a nonnegative R-supermartingale. For deterministic weights pi_k>=0 with sum pi_k<=1, M^R_t=sum_k pi_k Ltilde^R_{k,t} is an R-supermartingale with initial value <=1. Therefore E_t=inf_{R in P} M^R_t is a P-e-process because E_t<=M^R_t for every R. Thresholding E_t at 1/alpha gives sup_{R in P} P_R(sup_t E_t>=1/alpha)<=alpha.
derived_results.scope: Requires proper predictable densities, absolute continuity for the likelihood ratios, deterministic/non-data-adaptive start/expiry/weight design in this proof, and no recycling of killed weight back to one.

derived_results.claim: If all not-yet-split candidate laws share the same pre-split predictor, infinitely many future candidate starts collapse to one tail term, while deterministic expiry gives history-independent active state.
derived_results.derivation: For s_k>t, L^R_{k,t}=L^{-R}_t is identical. Hence M^R_t = W_future(t)L^{-R}_t + sum_{k: s_k<=t<e_k} pi_k L^R_{k,t}, with W_future(t)=sum_{k:s_k>t}pi_k. Expired candidates contribute zero and their capital is not reassigned. A scale with spacing g and lifetime H stores at most ceil(H/g) individualized candidate states plus the shared future-tail state. Multiple scales add these counts; if their pre-split predictors differ they require separate tail terms and explicit scale weights.

derived_results.claim: The r66 finite-sample segmented Gaussian lifetime formula must include the candidate's PFA start weight; omitting log(1/pi_k) materially understates weak-change lifetime requirements.
derived_results.derivation: From r66, for known variance Gaussian pure blocks with prefix length T, local length n, information I=delta^2/2, kappa in (0,1), confidence x=log(4/eta), and code regrets r_T,r_n: log C_{k,t} >= (1-kappa)I*T*n/(T+n) - (r_T+r_n+2x/kappa) with probability >=1-eta for the single-split composite e-value C_{k,t}=inf_mu L^mu_{k,t}. Since the global detector E_t>=pi_k C_{k,t}, threshold 1/alpha requires log C_{k,t}>=log(1/alpha)+log(1/pi_k). Define B_k=[log(1/(alpha pi_k))+r_T+r_n+2x/kappa]/[(1-kappa)I]. If B_k<T, n>=B_k*T/(T-B_k) is sufficient; if B_k>=T, this certificate cannot guarantee crossing at any finite n. Thus late-start prior mass, not just alpha, is part of the finite-threshold capacity condition.

derived_results.claim: The frozen-anchor full-prefix split process does not inherit the standard unit-weight ARL e-detector theorem, because adding a process only at its split injects data-dependent wealth accumulated before that split.
derived_results.counterexample: Let A be F_1-measurable with P(A)=1/2. Candidate 1 is constant wealth 1. Candidate 2 is a valid full-sequence martingale with L_0=1 and L_t=2*1_A for all t>=1. Pretend candidate 2 'starts' at s=2 and form D_1=1, D_2=1+L_2. For stopping time tau=2 on A and tau=1 otherwise, E[tau]=1.5 but E[D_tau]=0.5*3+0.5*1=2, violating the e-detector inequality E[D_tau]<=E[tau]. The issue is precisely that L_2 had already bet on the prefix before being added. Normalizing by L_{s,s-1} restores delayed-process validity but cancels the scored prefix factor and therefore loses the two-segment information advantage; an ARL-optimal version must return to a genuinely delayed/two-start construction or prove a different capital-accounting theorem.
derived_results.implication: Frozen-anchor segmented evidence is presently a PFA-mode architecture, not a drop-in ARL replacement. PFA<=alpha trivially implies infinite extended ARL under the no-change law when alpha<1, but that is not the finite-ARL design semantics used by classical e-detectors and carries the changepoint-time prior penalty.

derived_results.claim: A simple exactly normalized deterministic start prior reduces the late-start penalty from about 2 log k to log k + 2 log log k while retaining a closed-form future tail.
derived_results.derivation: For candidate index k>=1, set pi_k = log(2)*(1/log(k+1)-1/log(k+2)). The series telescopes to 1, its future tail after K started candidates is log(2)/log(K+2), and pi_k is asymptotically log(2)/(k log^2 k). This is computationally convenient because the unspawned future mass remains one scalar and matches the known PFA asymptotic need for a roughly log-time start penalty rather than the quadratic-prior 2 log k penalty.

derived_results.claim: A finite-memory frozen-anchor PFA detector retained strong-shift power with tens rather than hundreds/thousands of active split states, while weak shifts required longer lifetimes; the heavier-tail prior improved delay and completion rate.

details.model: Known-variance Gaussian observations. Composite no-change null N(mu,1), unknown mu. Each split alternative uses independent Normal(0,4) priors for the pre and post segment means, so each segmented numerator is a proper marginal density and the denominator is the maximized stationary Gaussian likelihood. Threshold alpha=0.05. Deterministic split schedules. Expired terms are killed, never renormalized. All configurations used common random paths.
details.paths: 300 no-change paths of length 1200; 300 change paths with 500 N(0,1) observations followed by 700 N(delta,1) observations for delta=1; the same 300 pre/post noise paths shifted by delta=0.5 for the weak-change condition.
details.state_interpretation: At H=300, g=8 needs at most ceil(300/8)=38 active split states plus a future-tail state; g=16 needs at most 19 plus a tail, versus up to 1200 split states for the all-start finite-horizon implementation. The zero observed false alarms are only a smoke test; formal PFA control comes from r67a, not from 300 null paths.
details.negative_condition: H=120 is inadequate for the tested delta=0.5 weak shift despite remaining formally PFA-valid: it detected only 104/300 within the 700-observation post-change horizon. Validity and power/lifetime are separate.

candidates_new.mechanism: Use a deterministic sparse start schedule, a summable start prior, a common pre-split predictor, proper reset post-split predictors, deterministic candidate expiry, and the outer infimum only after forming each null-specific weighted wealth. Aggregate all future unsplit candidates as one tail state; never renormalize expired capital.
candidates_new.formal_evidence: Composite-null PFA<=alpha follows from weighted killed null-specific supermartingales and pointwise domination by the outer-infimum process. The heavy-tail telescoping prior has exact normalization/tail and lower late-start penalty than 1/[k(k+1)].
candidates_new.empirical_evidence: In the stated Gaussian experiment, g16/H300/logheavy used <=19 active split states plus tail, matched the all-start median/q90 delay for delta=1, and retained 278/300 weak-shift detections versus 300/300 for all-start; all tested null paths had no alarm.
candidates_new.scope: PFA mode only at present; deterministic schedule/expiry; Gaussian Monte Carlo is engineering evidence, not a guarantee; weak-change lifetime and unknown-variance behavior remain open.
candidates_new.confidence: high for PFA validity, medium for the current finite-memory power design.

candidates_new.mechanism: Treat frozen-anchor segmented mixtures as a PFA-oriented detector and retain genuinely delayed e-detectors for finite-ARL mode. Do not claim a single architecture has both guarantees unless the capital accounting is proved.
candidates_new.formal_evidence: The explicit preloaded-wealth counterexample shows the standard ARL sum proof fails for full-prefix split wealth, whereas the weighted full-law mixture remains a valid PFA e-process.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The frozen-anchor segmented product can simply replace the original non-partitioned detector for both ARL and PFA.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. PFA closes cleanly; standard finite-ARL aggregation fails because each split candidate already contains prefix wealth before its nominal start.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Deterministic expiry can safely recycle the expired candidate's prior weight into a fresh start at wealth one.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected for the present theorem. Killing is safe because it only decreases wealth. Resetting/reassigning spent weight to one creates new capital and invalidates the PFA mixture unless a separate martingale reinvestment construction carries the current wealth rather than resetting it.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Sparse starts require an extra multiplicity threshold merely because there are multiple scales/times.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not if all starts/scales are assigned one globally summable deterministic prior before monitoring; their multiplicity is already paid through pi_{j,k}. Independent post-hoc detector families or data-adaptive start selection still need their own validity accounting.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Short lifetime is harmless once PFA validity is proved.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected for power: g8/H120 remained valid but detected only 104/300 of the tested delta=0.5 paths within 700 post-change observations.

frontier: Extend r67a from deterministic start/expiry schedules to a rigorously safe predictable allocation rule if possible, without letting data-dependent start weights correlate with already accumulated prefix wealth.

Derive the unknown-mean/unknown-variance frozen-anchor PFA detector with a proper initialization and source-qualified logarithmic universal-code regret; carry the candidate weight penalty log(1/pi_k) through the finite-sample lifetime inversion.

Optimize a multiscale schedule jointly over information floor I_j, spacing g_j, lifetime H_j and scale/start prior pi_{j,k}; prove a constant-factor detection-delay approximation while keeping active state O(sum_j H_j/g_j) and the PFA prior globally summable.

Build a matched finite-ARL comparator using genuinely delayed/two-start e-processes and quantify when the frozen-anchor PFA mode's stronger two-segment evidence outweighs its unavoidable changepoint-time prior penalty.

Stress variance-only and joint mean/variance changes with at least hundreds of common-random paths and verify that weak-shift misses are predicted by the weight-aware finite-sample capacity condition rather than by an implementation artifact.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Closed a composite-null PFA theorem for frozen-anchor segmented predictive laws with deterministic sparse starts and expiry.
Found the exact future-tail collapse that permits finite active state without approximating the PFA statistic before expiry.
Inserted the missing log(1/pi_k) start-weight cost into the finite-sample lifetime formula.
Constructed a concrete counterexample showing why full-prefix split wealth cannot inherit the usual finite-ARL sum theorem.
Derived an exactly normalized log-heavy telescoping start prior and tested it against the quadratic prior.
Ran 300-null plus 600-change common-random Monte Carlo per configuration and quantified state/power tradeoffs.

exact_next_action: Construct the unknown-variance version of the finite-memory frozen-anchor PFA detector and carry the start-prior penalty through its explicit finite-sample certificate. In parallel, formulate the multiscale design as an optimization over {I_j,g_j,H_j,pi_jk}: minimize worst-case delay subject to globally summable PFA mass and an active-state budget, then compare against a genuinely delayed ARL detector under matched Gaussian mean/variance changes.
